answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that scales with the value of work it takes on, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake agents. Newcomers start with small tasks and low trust, and must complete a long voyage of verified jobs before earning larger rewards, while misbehavior slashes the stake. Each fake identity must wander through the same costly history and lock its own pigment of capital — traceable funds that cannot be reused across identities — so building an army of sock puppets costs more than any reward it could extract.
